summary:
The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and the code of practice on single-sex services issued under it do not extend automatically to Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha. The territory's own statutes govern, and United Kingdom measures reach it only when applied by Order in Council. A visitor should expect local ordinances and local practice, not the United Kingdom framework, to determine how services, records and complaints are handled.

Consensual same-sex sexual activity has been lawful in the territory since 2001, and the age of consent is equalised at 16 across Saint Helena, Ascension Island and Tristan da Cunha.

The St Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha Constitution Order 2009 prohibits discrimination on grounds that include sexual orientation, in force since 2009. Its definition of discriminatory treatment covers different treatment on grounds such as sex, sexual orientation, race, colour, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, association with a national minority, property, age, disability, birth or other status. No extension of that ban to gender reassignment is documented.

Transgender people nonetheless fall within the remit of the territory's equality body. The Equality and Human Rights Commission in Saint Helena monitors human rights laws, promotes understanding of equality and works to eliminate unlawful discrimination, and it may conduct inquiries and investigations into suspected unlawful acts, including discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender reassignment. The Commission for Equality and Human Rights Ordinance 2015 defines gender reassignment as an intended, current or past process, or part of a process, for the purpose of reassigning a person's sex by changing physiological or other attributes of sex, or the state of mind whereby a person psychologically identifies with a gender inconsistent with, or not culturally associated with, their assigned sex at birth.

No transgender-specific criminal, documentation, screening, facilities, custody, care or violence provisions are documented for the territory. No transgender-specific marriage, adoption or penalty provisions are documented either.

Marriage is open to two people of the same sex on all three islands, legislated separately in each. The Marriage (Ascension) Ordinance 2016 commenced on 1 January 2017. The Marriages (Tristan da Cunha) Ordinance 2017 took effect on 4 August 2017 and defines marriage as the union of two persons regardless of sex, extending eligibility, formalities, rights and recognition to same-sex couples on equal terms with opposite-sex couples; its terms do not turn on the parties' recorded sex. The Marriage Ordinance 2017 took effect in Saint Helena on 20 December 2017, and the first same-sex marriage there was solemnised on 31 December 2018.

Adoption is open to single and married people regardless of sexual orientation under the Saint Helena Welfare of Children Ordinance 2010, which covers Saint Helena and Tristan da Cunha, and the Ascension Island Child Welfare Ordinance 2011. One source dates the availability of adoption by same-sex couples to 2017, while the governing ordinances are dated 2010 and 2011.
tangentialFactors: The three marriage ordinances followed separate legislative routes rather than a single territory-wide instrument. The Ascension Island Council approved its ordinance on 31 May 2016 by a vote of 5-0; it was signed and gazetted on 20 June 2016 and commenced on 1 January 2017.
localsOnly:
Adoption eligibility for residents is set by the Saint Helena Welfare of Children Ordinance 2010, covering Saint Helena and Tristan da Cunha, and the Ascension Island Child Welfare Ordinance 2011, covering Ascension Island. Single and married people may adopt regardless of sexual orientation. A 2006 United Kingdom Government report recorded no adoptions in Saint Helena or Ascension Island over many preceding years.

Residents can bring complaints of unlawful discrimination to the Equality and Human Rights Commission in Saint Helena, which may conduct inquiries and investigations into suspected unlawful acts.
outOfScopeNotes:
The territory is recorded in a 2013 source as an Overseas Country or Territory of the European Union with EU Charter applicability. The sources reviewed do not establish whether that association and charter applicability persist.

Whether the Constitution Order 2009 discrimination ban reaches gender reassignment is not documented; the order's enumerated grounds name sexual orientation and other statuses but not gender reassignment. The absence of transgender-specific criminal, documentation, screening, facilities, custody, care, violence, marriage, adoption and penalty provisions in the sources is an absence of documentation, not a verified statement that no such provisions exist.
